find_emojis.description: Find the emoji for a word: 'pizza' gives 🍕, 'rocket' gives 🚀. The single best match comes back on its own as well as in the list, so a step that just needs one emoji can take it straight. EmojiHub's own search only finds names containing your words exactly, so this widens the search when that comes up short - which is what makes 'smile' find the smiling faces too - and orders the results so the plainest match is first. Narrow it to a category or group to search one part of the catalogue.
find_emojis.name: find_emojis

parameters.description: The word or words to look for in emoji names. One plain word works best.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only use emojis from this part of the catalogue. Pick a broad category such as 'Food and drink', or one of the narrower groups inside it such as 'Smileys and people › Cat face' - the same field takes either, so you never have to work out which of the two you picked. Leave it empty to use every emoji.
parameters.name: category

parameters.description: How many emojis to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 10. The total number of matches is always reported, however many are returned.
parameters.name: limit

also_known_as.description: The emoji's other names, where it has any: 'slice of pizza' is also just 'pizza'. Searching matches either spelling.

find_related_emojis.description: Find the rest of the family for an emoji you already have. Give it a name - usually one an earlier step returned - and get back the others that share a word with it, without the one you started from: 'cat face' becomes a row of cats, 'grinning face' the rest of the smileys. Use it to build a set of reactions from a single emoji, or to offer alternatives to the one a search found.

description: Get the right emoji, as an emoji. EmojiHub is a free public catalogue of every standard emoji, and every action here hands back the character itself - 🎉, ready to drop straight into a Slack message, an email subject or a page title - along with its name and its HTML code. Search for one by word, draw one at random so a daily post never looks the same twice, pull a set of different ones for a poll or a row of reactions, browse a category such as Food and drink or a narrower group such as Cat face, or find the rest of the family for an emoji you already have. No account or API key required.
